result.summary: Release BLOCKED for Stage 16 (DDL-05, MIG-01, MIG-02, MIG-03). Read full requirement bodies/ACs from docs/requirements.yaml and cross-checked against tests/specs/*.md and the actual Zig test source (not just spec claims). DDL-05 (AC1-4 covered, AC5 legitimately out of scope pending DDL-01), MIG-01 (AC1-5 all covered), and MIG-03 (AC1-3/5 covered, AC4 legitimately out of scope pending the onboarding module) are clean. MIG-02 is not: AC4 ("the failure-recording transaction itself fails -> row remains pending") has NO test evidence anywhere in tests/reports/report-20260811-WF02-batch-0.yaml or the underlying test files. tests/specs/MIG-02.md's own Coverage note documents this as a deliberate deferral ("recorded as a known, narrow, non-blocking gap... revisit when MIG-04's implementation lands"), not a scope boundary to a different, not-yet-built requirement the way DDL-05 AC5 / MIG-03 AC4 are. The code AC4 describes (recordFailureSeparately, logSwallowedFailure in src/platform/migration_fanout.zig) IS delivered in this batch. Per docs/anti-patterns.md and this role's directive, a MUST requirement with any AC lacking passing integration test evidence must FAIL, regardless of how well-documented the deferral is. MIG-02 AC5 (structural, no-cross-connection-write) is a genuine inspection-only invariant (not runtime-observable) and is not itself blocking. Migration idempotency CONFIRMED: ran zig build migrate twice with BPM_TEST_DB_URL/BPM_DB_URL set explicitly in PowerShell -- both runs report 1144_platform_migrations_control_table.sql as "skip" and "No new migrations to apply.", exit code 0 on the second run. No MUST requirement test is skipped via error.SkipZigTest anywhere in this batch's files (grep-confirmed zero matches); the 64 skipped tests in the unit-full layer are pre-existing and unrelated to DDL-05/MIG-01/MIG-02/MIG-03. HTTP NFR benchmarks confirmed not applicable -- this batch adds no new HTTP endpoints (the admin surface is MIG-04/05/06, a separate later batch) -- noted explicitly rather than silently skipped.

issues.description: MIG-02 AC4 has no passing integration test evidence in this batch. tests/specs/MIG-02.md documents it as a deliberate same-batch deferral, not an out-of-scope boundary to a different requirement. Recommend either adding a narrow test-only fault-injection seam to exercise recordFailureSeparately's own failure path (BACKEND-DEV), or formally re-scoping AC4 out of MIG-02 into its own tracked requirement the way DDL-05 AC5 / MIG-03 AC4 were handled (REQ-ANALYST), routed via ORCH.

result.next_action: Route back to ORCH -- dispatch BACKEND-DEV (close MIG-02 AC4 test gap) or REQ-ANALYST (re-scope AC4), then re-run TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and TEST-RUNNER before RELEASE-VALIDATOR reconsiders Stage 16.
